Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E023.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:

  - comment: Kathryn Bishop (E023) is a contractor (Engineer). Contractors may have read by default; write requires advanced security training, which is not in HR's record. Recommend read unless Security confirms advanced training.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record confirms E023 is a contractor with basic security training. Write requires advanced training, so the maximum allowed access is read.
reason: Kathryn Bishop (E023) is a contractor with basic security training (per Security). Contractors may have read by default, and write requires advanced security training, which she does not have. The requested write level exceeds the maximum allowed (read), so grant the maximum of read.

content.text:
Kathryn Bishop (E023), contractor, Engineer role. Requesting write access to Payroll.

Policy: contractors can have read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

Security record: basic security training. So maximum is read. Requested write > max read, so grant read.

Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist role - Engineer doesn't own it, but that only matters for admin; irrelevant here.

Decision: read.
